items.title: Verstappen wins the rain-delayed Sprint as Russell crashes from the lead and the McLarens collide
items.summary: The Race and Formula1.com report that Verstappen won after Russell jumped him at the start but crashed at the end of lap one. Hamilton took second from a lightning start, Leclerc was third and Antonelli fourth. Norris hit team-mate Piastri at Turn 5 on the last lap: Piastri retired and Norris, eighth, is under investigation. Lawson was fifth and Bearman sixth, and Albon and Bortoleto collided before the safety car ended, an incident also to be investigated. There were nine retirements.
items.why_it_matters: Russell is out of the Sprint and already carries a 40-place power-unit grid drop for the Race, so it is hard to see him recovering much. The Norris/Piastri and Albon/Bortoleto investigations may change the points order; check the FIA documents before quoting the final Sprint classification.

items.title: Verstappen takes Sprint pole at 1:31.156 and keeps it after a yellow-flag hearing
items.summary: The Race says Verstappen needed one lap in SQ3 for the first Sprint pole of his season, 0.120s clear of Russell's older-spec Mercedes. He had been summoned for passing Hamilton between Turns 7 and 8 under single waved yellows after Perez hit the barriers at Turn 5 in SQ1. FIA Doc 29 records that Car 3 overtook Car 44 under single yellow flags and that no penalty was applied; Formula1.com explains why he avoided one.
items.why_it_matters: Verstappen starts the Sprint from pole with the stewards' decision recorded. The Race reports the pass breached the yellow-flag rules even though the FIA applied no penalty, so keep the stewards' wording separate from commentary on it.

items.title: Mercedes' old-spec car beats the new one: Russell fastest in practice and P2 in Sprint Qualifying, Antonelli P7
items.summary: Mercedes split their aero packages, with Russell on the older specification and Antonelli on the update. Russell topped the only practice session; Antonelli was seventh, 1.3s slower, though The Race says the two ran very different programmes. In Sprint Qualifying Russell took P2 and said the old car is not bad, while Antonelli, P7, called the new-spec car very difficult to drive.
items.why_it_matters: It tests whether the upgrade helped or hurt, and Mercedes carry the question into the Sprint. Treat the one-hour practice comparison cautiously because the programmes differed.

items.title: FIA Doc 20: Russell's new power-unit elements carry a 40-place grid drop for the next Race
items.summary: Mercedes confirmed on 7 October that Russell would take a penalty after his power-unit failure late in the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The FIA's power-unit document lists the penalty as a drop of 40 grid positions in the next Race in which he participates.
items.why_it_matters: The penalty is recorded against the Race grid, not the Sprint grid. Confirm the Sprint and Race starting grids once the FIA publishes them.

items.title: Rivals reject Williams' cost-cap catch-up proposal ahead of the November F1 Commission
items.summary: The Race reports Williams looks set to fall short of the support needed to change the 2027 cost-cap rules, with key rivals opposed. It is expected to go to a team vote at the next F1 Commission meeting, and The Race separately reports that Vowles is confident of the votes and that Red Bull is pivotal to the timing.
items.why_it_matters: A proposal, not a rule change, and the reports conflict on whether it has the votes. Attribute each claim to The Race.
